overall.summary: All six tools broadly implement what their descriptions state, but several undocumented constraints and behaviours exist: read_query enforces a SELECT-only check, write_query silently accepts DDL statements beyond INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, describe_table interpolates user input directly into SQL creating an injection risk, and append_insight triggers an MCP network notification to clients. No declared effect is entirely absent from the implementation.

startup.behaviour: Creates parent directories for the database file path if they do not exist (mkdir parents=True)
Opens (and implicitly creates) the SQLite database file on disk at the configured path
A ServerWrapper instance is instantiated at module import time with a hardcoded 'test.db' path
On Windows, reconfigures stdin/stdout/stderr to UTF-8 encoding if PYTHONIOENCODING is unset
Registers a memo://insights resource and an mcp-demo prompt in addition to the tools

undocumented_behaviours.behaviour: Appends the insight to an in-memory list (db.insights) that persists only for the server process lifetime; insights are not written to the database
Sends an MCP resource-updated notification for memo://insights to all connected clients
Calls _synthesize_memo() and discards the result (side-effect-free call, but synthesises memo in memory)
Rejects any query that does not begin with CREATE TABLE, raising a ValueError returned as an error message
undocumented_behaviours.evidence: server.py: handle_call_tool/if not arguments['query'].strip().upper().startswith('CREATE TABLE'): raise ValueError

undocumented_behaviours.behaviour: Returns fixed string 'Table created successfully' instead of row/schema details
Uses PRAGMA table_info with the table name interpolated directly into the SQL string without parameterisation (SQL injection risk)
Queries sqlite_master system table specifically; result also includes any SQLite internal or view entries that match type='table'
undocumented_behaviours.evidence: server.py: handle_call_tool/db._execute_query("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'")

undocumented_behaviours.behaviour: Rejects any query that does not begin with SELECT, raising a ValueError returned as an error message
Opens a new SQLite connection per call (no persistent connection pool); each call opens and closes a file handle
Rejects SELECT queries explicitly, raising a ValueError returned as an error message
Also accepts and executes CREATE, DROP, ALTER statements (not only INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) because _execute_query commits on those prefixes too
Returns the number of affected rows, not the modified data
